A principal produced by another JwtAccessTokenService instance is not accepted by the canonical verifier, even for the same subject.
Reflected principals, identity grants and token issuers cannot create accepted principals or tokens for caller-selected subjects.
All failures, logs and toString output redact tokens, subjects, signing material and identity bytes.
No session membership, route, JDBC, schema, duel transition or persistence implementation is introduced in this prerequisite.

tasks.title: S25B canonical session authority and authoritative transition after auth and mutable-digit prerequisites
tasks.summary: Introduce the production-owned canonical session authority and server-authoritative application boundary after the authentication and mutable-digit contracts are integrated.
acceptance_criteria: External commands contain only typed intent and never caller-authored snapshot, event, score, phase, winner or result.
The application service binds a trusted actor to a session participant, loads current state, enforces phase and turn ownership, and computes the transition with the authoritative duel aggregate.
Only an internally constructed validated transition can cross into persistence.

The repository port and validated transition contain no plaintext secret, raw guess, SensitiveDuelDigits or replayable raw aggregate history; only validated viewer-neutral public state, ordered event, result, revision and server-derived fingerprint may cross the persistence boundary.

No raw String or UUID factory can mint a trusted actor. Actor binding must consume an authentication-bound principal capability and verify current session membership; if current auth contracts cannot prove that boundary, stop with needs_worker_fix instead of inventing trust.

Production composition owns the trusted JwtAccessTokenService, concrete server-owned membership source, canonical resolver and downstream authoritative consumer together; callers cannot inject a membership authority or resolver.
No exported, package-visible, protected, Kotlin internal, synthetic or default factory or constructor accepts a caller-owned SessionMembershipPort, membership record, resolver or capability.

A genuine production-composed positive path succeeds, while caller-owned ports or records, foreign resolvers, reflected resolvers, synthetic membership records, reflected capabilities, wrong sessions, wrong members, duplicates and membership-limit violations fail closed.

Javap and hostile reflection tests enumerate every constructor, synthetic constructor, default bridge and mangled Kotlin internal method on the session-authorization and production-composition boundary.
Secret and guess command values are never copied into additional immutable Strings, logs, snapshots, events, results or persistence records; mutable temporary buffers are zeroed in finally.
Adversarial tests reject spoofed actors, stale revisions, out-of-turn moves, forged outcomes, config/history mutation and commands after terminal phase.
Domain and application responsibilities remain in focused files and no new production file exceeds 400 lines.
